reason: Both meet all hard requirements equally well, but Response B is more rigorous: it pairs each phase's entry criterion with an explicit, quantified exit criterion (e.g., reconciliation match rate ≥99.9% for N consecutive days), states cumulative percentages to avoid ambiguity, and cleanly isolates decommissioning into a distinct future Phase 4 with its own criteria rather than just noting it as out of scope. Its halt metrics also include more concrete, multi-signal thresholds (reconciliation mismatch, failed-payment delta, support ticket surge), giving a more actionable and auditable rollout plan.
